ety.text: First attested in 1806. бе́лый (bélyj) + -о- (-o-) + шве́йка (švéjka), calque of German Weißnäherin.

s.g: initialism of вооружённые си́лы (vooružónnyje síly, “armed forces”)

ety.text: From встряхну́ть (vstrjaxnútʹ) + -ка (-ka), but constructed as if from *встрясти́ (compare imperfective трясти́ (trjastí), perfective тряхну́ть (trjaxnútʹ)).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gorditi, from *gordъ. By surface analysis, го́род (górod) + -и́ть (-ítʹ).

s.g: to (try to) achieve, to attain, to get, to reach
to permit, to allow, to tolerate

x: уничтоже́ние живо́й си́лы и те́хники проти́вника

ety.text: Literally, “live force”. Compare Ukrainian жива́ си́ла (žyvá sýla), Belarusian жыва́я сі́ла (žyvája síla), Polish siła żywa, Bulgarian жи́ва си́ла (žíva síla). Compare also French forces vives.
Syllabic abbreviation of заве́дующий скла́дом (zavédujuščij skládom).
Borrowed from German Salve, from Latin salve.

s.g: Used to emphasise, clarify or confirm the meaning or identity of the following word or what comes later and sometimes can be rather difficult to translate into English. Often translated with a word order involving "it was [this] that", "[this] is what", "[this] is the one that" etc., otherwise "exactly", "precisely", "just", "specifically", etc. or not translated.
x: Статья́ появи́лась в газе́те и́менно в пя́тницу.
Всё произошло́ и́менно так, как я и предполага́л.

s.g: namely, specifically, which is/are, to wit; used to specify something or to enumerate a list.
x: В году́ четы́ре сезо́на, а и́менно — весна́, ле́то, о́сень и зима́.
В тот день, а и́менно в суббо́ту, произошло́ ЧП.

s.g: exactly, that's right, right, precisely, indeed; used to emphasise agreement or confirmation.
x: — Мы же договори́лись сде́лать э́то. — И́менно, поэ́тому мы э́то и де́лаем.
— Вы мне э́то говори́те? — И́менно, Вам!

s.g: Indianapolis (the capital city of Indiana, United States)
to defecate (to empty the bowels of feces)
by the way, incidentally, side note (in connection with what has just been said, in addition to what has already been said)

in a word, so to speak, just saying, if I/we may say so, dare I/we say, it must be said, I have to say (used to introduce and highlight the expressivity of a summary or description of something already talked about)
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see к (k), сло́ву (slóvu).

ety.text: Borrowed from English Cowper, from Edward Cowper.

s.g: it's what is used to buy: деньги.

x: Карлик поднял палец и спросил: «Построю лабиринт, в котором смогу затеряться с тем, кто захочет меня найти, — кто это сказал и о чём?»

s.g: big club, battle axe (16th to 18th century)
to force, to coerce, to constrain

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic насиловати (nasilovati), from Proto-Slavic *nasilovati.

s.g: to write or draw by scratching
to write or draw carelessly or illegibly
to wipe off, to dry off
to discover that Queen Anne's dead (to rediscover and announce common knowledge)

ety.text: Literally, “to discover America.”. Compare Polish odkrywać Amerykę, Italian scoprire l'America, French redécouvrir l'Amérique.

x: Ты́сячи бе́женцев при́были из Ве́нгрии в А́встрию.

s.g: to increase, to rise, to grow
to rise, to swell (water), to wax (moon)

ety.text: From при- (pri-) + быть (bytʹ). Compare Czech přibýt and Polish przybyć.

s.g: to drill a hole in, to perforate
to twist (something) through (something) (esp. meat through a meat grinder)
pejorative of рабо́та (rabóta): nasty work, nasty job

x: Было у них и немного рыбок: благословив, Он велел раздать и их.

s.g: belly-god, a term of abuse for someone who eats a great quantity of food in one sitting

ety.text: рот (rot, “mouth”) + -а́н (-án, augmentative suffix) by its voracious appearance and behaviour.

s.g: a male given name, equivalent to English Sextus

syllogism (argument whose conclusion is supported by two premises, of which one contains the term that is the predicate of the conclusion, and the other contains the term that is the subject of the conclusion)

ety.text: Borrowed from French symboliste, influenced by си́мвол (símvol).

x: Россия, я — твой капиллярный сосудик, мне больно когда — тебе больно, Россия.

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic сърокъ (sŭrokŭ), original meaning "agreement", from Proto-Slavic *sъrokъ.
Borrowed from Japanese 豊見城 (とみぐすく, Tomigusuku).

s.g: Shenzhen (a major subprovincial city in southern Guangdong, China)
